description: Guided B2 content batch for The Sound Maze. Each target is spoken aloud; the learner selects its spelling. Draft content is not wired into the live game.

questions.explain: Candid has the short /æ/ vowel in its first stressed syllable. Candy and candle also begin with /kænd/, but candid has a different ending; kindle begins with /ɪ/.
Plummet has /ʌ/ in its first syllable. Plumage has /uː/, planet has /æ/, and plumb is a shorter word with a different ending.
Tenet has /ɛ/ in its first syllable. Tenant has /ɛ/ too but a different second syllable; tenor has /ɛ/ followed by /nər/, and tender ends with a different consonant sequence.
Rhetoric begins with /r/; the written rh is pronounced /r/. Ethics begins with a vowel, lethargy with /l/, and method with /m/.
Chasm begins with /k/ although it is spelled ch. Sham begins with /ʃ/, champ with /tʃ/, and ham with /h/.
Gnarled begins with /n/ because the written g is silent. Garbled begins with /g/, hardy with /h/, and marble with /m/.
Drowned ends with /nd/. Drown ends with /n/, drowsy with /zi/, and drowning with /ɪŋ/.
Depth ends with /θ/. Debt ends with /t/, dense with /s/, and desk with /sk/.
Prompt ends with /mpt/. Prom ends with /m/, pronged with /ŋdʒd/, and promise with /s/.
Maintenance is pronounced /ˈmeɪntənəns/. Maintain ends with /eɪn/, maintained ends with /eɪnd/, and mountain begins with /maʊn/.
Privilege is pronounced /ˈprɪvəlɪdʒ/. Village begins with /v/, pilgrimage has a different first syllable and stress pattern, and percentage begins with /pər/.
Rhythm is pronounced /ˈrɪðəm/; y represents the vowel sound. Ribbon, ridden, and written have different medial consonants and vowel patterns.
